system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
## Buyer-side review — Project Kestrel

*This review is necessarily subject to the full SPA, funds flow and underlying DD-002–DD-012 documents.*

| Issue | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation — one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% of price / AUD 4.8m**. | A materially higher cap—preferably **50% / AUD 12m** absent adequate W&I insurance—with separate treatment for fundamental, tax and specific indemnity claims. | **Reject 20% and counter at 50%:** AUD 4.8m may be inadequate for systemic warranty breaches in a AUD 24m acquisition. |
| **SPA-N-002 De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 deductible basket, with only excess recoverable. | Lower thresholds, aggregation of related claims, and a **tipping basket** once reached; propose AUD 15,000 de minimis and AUD 150,000 basket. | **Counter and require related claims to aggregate:** the proposed deductible structure leaves the Buyer bearing the first AUD 250,000 of otherwise valid loss. |
| **SPA-N-003 General claims time limit** | General Warranty Claims must be notified within **18 months**; Seller seeks to extend limitation language to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | At least **24 months** for general warranties, with longer bespoke periods for tax, title, IP and indemnities. | **Counter at 24 months and confine it to general warranties:** 18 months may not cover two audit/reporting cycles and must not become a universal bar. |
| **SPA-N-004 Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to the same 20% cap, thresholds and 18-month limit as general warranties. | Liability up to **100% of the purchase price**, no de minimis/basket, and at least seven years or the maximum legally enforceable period. | **Reject general-warranty treatment:** the Buyer is paying AUD 24m for valid ownership and transfer of 100% of the shares. |
| **SPA-N-005 Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance clauses apply to all Claims; no express fraud carve-out is identified. | An express carve-out for fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation, wilful misconduct and deliberate concealment, including from caps, thresholds, time bars, disclosure and exclusive-remedy provisions. | **Insert a comprehensive fraud carve-out:** the Seller must not benefit from contractual protections where information was dishonestly withheld or misstated. |
| **SPA-N-006 Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the entire data room, Accounts, registers and public records. | Only matters **fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to identify their nature, scope and likely impact**, preferably against specified warranties; no general public-record disclosure. | **Reject clauses 1.1–1.2 as blanket disclosure:** dumping documents into a data room should not qualify warranties without clear and specific disclosure. |
| **SPA-N-007 Buyer knowledge qualifier** | Claims barred by Buyer/adviser knowledge, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records. | Delete the qualifier or restrict it to the **actual, conscious knowledge of named Buyer deal-team individuals**, without enquiry, constructive knowledge or adviser imputation. | **Delete or tightly narrow it:** constructive and adviser knowledge would improperly transfer disclosure and diligence risk to the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-008 Bluefen consent** | Seller to use reasonable endeavours; condition treated as satisfied upon delivery of written consent, although associated conditions remain unproven. | A Completion condition requiring final, effective and preferably unconditional consent, satisfaction of all conditions, and no adverse contract amendment or payment without Buyer approval. | **Do not waive or deem the condition satisfied prematurely:** Bluefen represents about 30% of FY26 revenue and its continuity is fundamental to value. |
| **SPA-N-009 Riverlark facility** | Approximately AUD 3.2m outstanding; release to follow Completion. | Repayment and irrevocable discharge of all debt, guarantees and security **at or simultaneously with Completion**, funded through an agreed payout direction and evidenced by executed releases. | **Make discharge a Completion deliverable and permit withholding:** a post-Completion promise is inconsistent with a debt-free acquisition and leaves the target encumbered. |
| **SPA-N-010 Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 Completion bonuses treated as a Seller matter and omitted from funds flow; on-costs are not addressed. | All bonuses and related payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs treated as Seller transaction expenses/debt-like items, paid or deducted at Completion, with an indemnity for any target liability. | **Deduct the full grossed-up amount from Seller proceeds:** Completion-triggered liabilities must not reduce the debt-free/cash-free value delivered to the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-011 Ironquay IP indemnity** | Existing indemnity limited to the particular SOW3 payment; AUD 180,000 remains recorded as open and ownership transfer is conditional on cleared payment. | Pre-Completion payment plus written confirmation/assignment of all Project Materials, or a specific indemnity covering payment, ownership, use, infringement, enforcement costs and resulting loss. | **Require cured title or a broad standalone indemnity:** paying only the fee does not itself prove that the target owns and can freely exploit the relevant IP. |
| **SPA-N-012 Export/privacy incident** | Characterised as preliminary and not expected to be material; access, scope, notification duties and loss remain unresolved. | Completed forensic/legal investigation, preservation of evidence, remediation and required notifications before Completion, plus a specific indemnity for all incident-related loss and regulatory exposure. | **Escalate and ring-fence the incident:** approximately 1,240 records may be affected and the current disclosure leaves both facts and exposure unknown. |
| **SPA-N-013 Sandbar renewals** | Three AUD 110,000 renewals—AUD 330,000 aggregate—characterised as ordinary-course operating costs. | Full contracts and renewal status, confirmation of termination rights and accounting treatment, Buyer consent before commitment, and adjustment for pre-Completion or non-ordinary obligations. | **Do not accept the characterisation without evidence:** the disclosure expressly does not establish that the renewals are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course. |
| **SPA-N-014 Category separation** | Caps, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions proposed to apply to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | Distinct regimes for general warranties, fundamental/title, tax, IP, specific indemnities, covenants and fraud, with separate caps, periods and baskets and no unintended cross-erosion. | **Rewrite the limitation architecture by claim category:** an “all Claims” formulation could neutralise specifically negotiated protections. |
| **SPA-N-015 Title verification** | Seller relies on DD-012 share register as evidence of ownership of 100% of the shares. | Constitution, historical allotment/transfer records, share certificates, ASIC records, PPSR and other encumbrance searches, beneficial-ownership confirmation, executed transfers and release of all security or third-party rights. | **Require a complete title and encumbrance package:** the company-maintained register alone does not establish an unbroken chain or clean, unencumbered title. |
| **SPA-N-016 Tax/IP open terms** | Seller says tax and IP warranty positions are settled under the general 20%/18-month regime. | A standalone tax covenant/deed with a 100% price cap and statutory assessment period plus buffer; robust IP ownership/non-infringement warranties and specific indemnities with higher caps and longer survival. | **Treat both regimes as open and reject general treatment:** tax and core IP exposures can be latent, high-value and discovered well after 18 months. |

### Immediate Buyer priorities

1. Make **Bluefen consent** and **Riverlark discharge** hard Completion conditions/deliverables.  
2. Deduct or fully provide for the **AUD 420,000 bonuses plus on-costs**.  
3. Resolve **Ironquay IP title** before Completion or obtain a comprehensive specific indemnity.  
4. Investigate and separately indemnify the **export/privacy incident**.  
5. Reject blanket disclosure, constructive knowledge and the proposed application of general limitations to every Claim.
=== END ADVICE ===
